explanation: An oxy-hydrogen flame played on quicklime, calcium oxide, which glowed a brilliant white. Theatres used limelight from the 1830s to pick out the star of the show.

claims.text: Limelight came from heating a block of quicklime (calcium oxide) in an oxy-hydrogen flame until it glowed.
Limelight did not come from heating a carbon rod, a platinum wire or lime-tree wood.
Theatres began using limelight in the 1830s.
The phrase 'in the limelight' comes from limelight used to pick out performers on stage.
